description: Before the MAX_EVENTS=100k/history cap, a reflective-infinite-medium k-eff hung (~9 CPU-min, one looping history). Find the geometry/nudge corner case (suspect: history stuck near a reflective plane/corner or coincident-surface re-cross in run_keff_csg) and fix properly; the cap currently leaks such histories (small bias).

notes.author: root@vm
notes.content: Root-cause analysis (2026-07-24, from the op-6tz.34 work). The reflective-corner stuck-history is grazing-incidence ping-pong: a particle moving nearly parallel to a reflective wall, near a corner, alternately hits the two/three perpendicular walls at sub-nudge distances. Each fixed 1e-9 cm nudge advances it only ~1e-9 cm ALONG the wall, so traversing an O(1 cm) feature needs ~1e9 bounces >> MAX_EVENTS=100k -> the history is capped and leaked (the band-aid). This is distinct from op-6tz.34 (now fixed): that was a lattice-edge/wall coincident tie leaking histories OUT of the box; this is in-corner non-progress. A PROPER fix (per this bead: do NOT extend the band-aid) needs OpenMC-style token-based surface tracking (advance exactly to the surface, resolve the next cell by surface index + sense, and compose a corner reflection off all coincident reflective surfaces in one event) rather than a fixed position nudge. That is a larger rework best done against the OpenMC reference source (not available in this sandbox), so leaving open with this analysis. The residual ~2% surface-vs-delta gap in the op-6tz.34 regression test is plausibly this effect.

notes.author: root@vm
notes.content: Root-cause fixed: new Geometry::compose_corner_reflection in geometry.rs, called from cross_surface reflective arm. At a reflective corner/edge (other reflective walls within 1e-9 cm of the crossing point) it now reflects off ALL coincident walls in one event (reflections compose at a corner = retroreflection) instead of ping-ponging 1e-9 cm/event. Sign-agnostic crossing test so min-side corners handled; lone-wall case bit-identical. Marked honestly as a robustness fix for this crate's fixed-nudge tracker (no C++ ref on host). Regression tests in triso.rs. Measured: grazing history 100003 events + 20 corner leaks to 4 events + 0 leaks; small U235 reflective cube surface 2.22235+/-0.00334 vs delta 2.21925+/-0.00320 = 0.67 sigma. Suite green: 95 lib + 26 notebooks, 0 fail. CAVEAT: worktree based on main, 658 behind develop; develop-only nested-lattice ~2pct residual not measurable here. Verified fix ports cleanly to develop (cross_surface + triso imports identical). Not committed.

notes.author: root@vm
notes.content: Fixed in 69d8874 (integrated onto claude/outram-mc-setup-cb1bg9, which has op-6tz.34). Root cause: cross_surface reflective arm reflected a grazing near-corner particle off only the primary wall; the fixed 1e-9 cm nudge left it headed into the perpendicular wall(s), re-crossing at sub-nudge distances (~1e5-1e9 events → MAX_EVENTS leak, negative bias). Fix: Geometry::compose_corner_reflection composes the specular reflection of every reflective/white/periodic surface coincident with the crossing point (|evaluate(r)|<=1e-9) that the particle actually crosses (|u·n|>0, sign-agnostic for min/max-side axis-aligned walls). Retroreflection at a right-angle corner → particle leaves in one event. Lone-wall case is bit-identical to surf.reflect. MAX_EVENTS/NUDGE untouched. Tests: corner_reflection_composes_at_exact_corner (unit), corner_grazing_history_terminates_without_pingpong (worst 100003→4 events, 20→0 leaks), corner_reflective_cube_surface_tracking_unbiased (surface 2.22235±0.00334 vs delta 2.21925±0.00320, 0.67σ). 158 lib + 30 notebook tests pass; op-6tz.34 nested-lattice test still green. CAVEAT: robustness fix for this crate's fixed-nudge tracker (not an OpenMC routine port — only the physics is mirrored); non-orthogonal corners compose order-dependently (approximate), axis-aligned cube/lattice corners exact.

description: Follow-up from op-u6s.7 (2026-07-17). The event-based batched-flight GPU path (run_keff_gpu_batched) puts the per-event flight (RNG+Sigma_t lookup+distance+streaming) on the GPU but keeps the branchy collision physics on the CPU, forcing a CPU/GPU round-trip (upload live batch, dispatch, read back pos+rng+outcome, CPU collide, re-upload) PER EVENT. Measured verdict: memory-transfer/launch bound, GPU ~4-5x SLOWER than CpuMultiThread at every batch size 1e3..1e6, no crossover. To actually beat multi-thread the collision kernel (nuclide sampling, reaction partition fission|capture|inelastic|n2n|elastic, secondary energy/angle laws, on-GPU fission banking + stream compaction) must run on the GPU too, so a batch advances through many events WITHOUT leaving GPU memory. Large, branch-heavy effort. Alternatively evaluate Woodcock/delta-tracking on GPU (single majorant, no per-nuclide branch) as a more GPU-friendly collision scheme.

notes.author: teddy0@snrsi-arch-desktop
notes.content: op-u6s.8 DONE (2026-07-17, RTX 3050). Ported collision physics onto the GPU: new fused flight+collision WGSL kernel (src/gpu/shaders/batched_event.wgsl) + host/CPU-mirror (src/gpu/batched_event.rs) + per-nuclide XS tabulation (src/gpu/collision_grid.rs). On GPU now (per event, f32, batch resident): nuclide sampling, reaction partition (fission|capture|inelastic|elastic; LOW-tier n2n=0), elastic two-body/exponential-mu kinematics, Weisskopf continuum inelastic, fission tagging. Only fission DAUGHTERS (count+chi+angle) stay on CPU, once per generation from the handed-back seed. run_keff_gpu now routes to run_keff_gpu_event. Whole generation stays GPU-resident: only a 4-byte live-count read per event + one fission read-back per generation. V&V: gpu_event_matches_cpu_mirror = 0/4096 mismatches, max_e_rel 5e-7; three_compute_modes k_gpu=1.01284+/-0.00823 vs k_single=1.00762+/-0.00827 (0.45 sigma). BENCHMARK (same-session before/after, Godiva LOW, 3+7 gen, 12-core): GPU 2.7-4.1x faster than collision-on-CPU path; deficit vs CpuMultiThread shrank ~6.6x->~1.9x at 1e6; GPU now beats CpuSingleThread for N>=1e5. VERDICT: NO crossover vs 12-core CpuMultiThread on RTX3050 (still ~1.9x slower at 1e6) - honest, no fabricated win. 95 lib tests pass (+5), android clean, 0 warnings. Dev log: crates/outram-mc-libs/docs/gpu_collision_dev_log.md; manifest: docs/ai-fleet-review/gpu-collision/REVIEW_MANIFEST.md.

title: outram-mc: move collision physics onto GPU to make batched transport win vs CpuMultiThread
